summary: Source decomposition of generalized Heegner cycles from Bertolini-Darmon-Prasanna (introduction read in full), Castella-Hsieh together with its published erratum (both read for the statements and corrections that the roadmap depends on), and Longo-Vigni (hypothesis package and main Lambda-adic theorem). Covers: the variety X_r = W_r x A^r with its proper smooth model over Z[1/N] and the resulting Bloch-Kato containment; the cycles Delta_phi indexed by isogenies, their homological triviality (with the r = 0 correction) and the Main Theorem relating a SPECIAL VALUE of the anticyclotomic p-adic L-function to the SQUARE of an Abel-Jacobi image, together with its scaling law under omega_A -> lambda omega_A; the three published corrections to Castella-Hsieh Sec. 7 (Lemma 7.5 needs L/Q_p unramified and is not known in the ramified case; Prop. 7.8's correct proof is Kobayashi-Ota's; Lemma 7.10 is about p-ramified ABELIAN extensions); Castella-Hsieh Thm. 4.9 with its interpolation range -r < j < r and Thm. 5.7 with the factor (-c_o^{r-1}), the order-two element sigma_{-1,p} and the t-power convention; Longo-Vigni's admissibility Def. 2.1 with the explicit exceptional set Xi, the exclusion of K = Q(i) and Q(sqrt(-3)), and Thm. 3.5's oriented divisibility; and Castella-Hsieh's Selmer consequences Thms. 6.1-6.4 with Thm. 6.3 in its CORRECTED form. GH.7 and GH.8 are not_read; GH.3 is only partially read. The load-bearing replacement proof (Kobayashi-Ota Lemma 4.10) and Hsieh's nonvanishing theorem were NOT read, although both sources are present in the library.

nodes.title: The variety X_r = W_r x A^r fibred over the modular curve, and its model over Z[1/N]
nodes.statement: Fix an imaginary quadratic field K, a CM elliptic curve A with complex multiplication by the full ring of integers O_K, defined over the Hilbert class field H of K, and a prime p not dividing N. Replace the (2r)-dimensional Kuga-Sato variety W_{2r} by the (2r+1)-dimensional variety X_r = W_r x A^r, where W_r is the r-th (desingularised) fibre power of the universal elliptic curve over the modular curve C. Like W_{2r}, the variety X_r is fibred over C and carries an infinite collection of special cycles defined over abelian extensions of K. As shown in the appendix of Bertolini-Darmon-Prasanna (by Brian Conrad), X_r admits a PROPER SMOOTH MODEL over Spec Z[1/N]; consequently, for F a finite extension of Q_p, the image of the etale Abel-Jacobi map is contained in the Bloch-Kato subspace H^1_f.
hypotheses: A has CM by the FULL ring of integers O_K and is defined over the Hilbert class field H, not merely over an arbitrary field with CM by an order
p does not divide N; this is what makes the good-reduction/smooth-proper statement available and what places the Abel-Jacobi image in H^1_f
W_r is the DESINGULARISED r-fold fibre product; the desingularisation is part of the construction and the smooth proper model of the appendix is for X_r, not for a naive fibre product

the dimension of X_r is 2r + 1, and the relevant Chow group is CH^{r+1}(X_r)_{0,Q}, with subscript 0 for homologically trivial and Q for rational coefficients -- the cycles are taken with RATIONAL coefficients throughout
proofSteps: Form the r-fold fibre power of the universal elliptic curve over C and desingularise, obtaining W_r; take the product with A^r.
The appendix constructs a proper smooth model of X_r over Spec Z[1/N].
Combine with the comparison theorems between p-adic etale cohomology and de Rham cohomology to convert the etale Abel-Jacobi map (0.0.1) into the p-adic one (0.0.2).
acceptance: Check the dimension count: X_r has dimension 2r + 1 and the cycles have codimension r + 1, so they are r-dimensional.
Check that the Bloch-Kato containment is a CONSEQUENCE of the smooth proper model over Z[1/N] and not an assumption.
Check that the coefficients are rational at this stage; the stage text warns that a class in rational cohomology is not automatically integral, and no integrality statement is made here.

nodes.title: The cycles Delta_phi, their homological triviality, and the p-adic Abel-Jacobi formula
nodes.statement: The generalized Heegner cycles are indexed by isogenies phi : A -> A'. The cycle Delta_phi attached to phi is supported on the fibre (A')^r x A^r above the point of C attached to A', and is essentially the r-fold self-product of the GRAPH of phi. Section 2.3 of Bertolini-Darmon-Prasanna establishes that the Delta_phi are HOMOLOGICALLY TRIVIAL. When r = 0 the cycle is a CM point on the modular curve C and one REPLACES Delta_phi by Delta_phi - infinity_1, where infinity_1 is any cusp; for r >= 1 no such correction is needed, because Prop. 2.4 (a computation of the projector epsilon_X on the de Rham cohomology of X_r) implies epsilon_X H^{2r+2}(X,Q) = 0. The homological-triviality statement itself is Prop. 2.7, not Prop. 2.4. The cycles are all defined over abelian extensions of K -- by Remark 2.6, over the compositum of the abelian extension over which the isomorphism class of (A,t_A) is defined with the ring class field H_c of conductor c -- so their images under the etale, p-adic and complex Abel-Jacobi maps are defined. Moreover Sec. 2.4 shows that the classical Heegner cycles on W_{2r} attached to K are the images of generalized Heegner cycles on X_{2r} under a suitable ALGEBRAIC CORRESPONDENCE, so the generalized cycles carry at least as much arithmetic information as the classical ones. The MAIN THEOREM (stated under three simplifying hypotheses, the general form being Thm. 5.13) reads: with Delta = Delta_1 the cycle attached to the identity isogeny, viewed in CH^{r+1}(X_r)_0(Q-bar_p)_Q, L_p(f, chi)/Omega_p^{2(r-2j)} = [(1 - chi-bar(p-bar) a_p + chi-bar(p-bar)^2 p^{k-1})/j!]^2 times AJ_{Q-bar_p}(Delta)(omega_f wedge omega_A^j eta_A^{r-j})^2; the analytic side is a SPECIAL VALUE of the p-adic L-series, not a derivative, and the algebraic side involves Abel-Jacobi IMAGES, not p-adic heights.
hypotheses: the three simplifying assumptions of the displayed Main Theorem are: (1) K has class number 1 and odd discriminant d_K < -3, with epsilon_K the associated odd Dirichlet character; (2) f lies in S_k(Gamma_0(N), epsilon_K^k), and d_K must divide N when k is odd; (3) the grossencharacter chi lies in Sigma^{(1)}_cc(N) and has the explicit form chi(alpha) = epsilon_K^k(alpha) alpha^{k-1-j} alpha-bar^{1+j} for some 0 <= j <= r. The general statement is Thm. 5.13

the character chi lies OUTSIDE the range of classical interpolation defining the anticyclotomic p-adic L-function L_p(f,chi); the classical value L(f, chi^{-1}, 0) vanishes but L_p(f,chi) is not forced to vanish
the formula depends on the choice of the differential omega_A: replacing omega_A by lambda omega_A multiplies BOTH sides by lambda^{2(2j-r)}, so the identity is equivariant rather than absolute

the two sides are SQUARES; the analytic side carries the square of the Euler-type factor and the square of the Abel-Jacobi pairing, which is the source of the distinction between the BDP distribution and its square

the case r = 0 needs the EXPLICIT correction Delta_phi - infinity_1 (subtract an arbitrary cusp) to make the CM point homologically trivial; for r >= 1 the cycle is already homologically trivial. In both cases the statement is Prop. 2.7; Prop. 2.4 is the cohomological input, not the statement
proofSteps: Define Delta_phi as (essentially) the r-fold self-product of the graph of phi inside the fibre (A')^r x A^r.
Prove homological triviality (Prop. 2.4 for r >= 1; a correction for r = 0), so that the Abel-Jacobi maps apply.
Compare with the classical Heegner cycles on W_{2r} via an algebraic correspondence (Sec. 2.4).
Compute AJ_{Q-bar_p}(Delta) by the Serre-Tate/rigid-analytic method of Sec. 3 and match it with the p-adic L-value; the proof occupies Secs. 3-5 and was NOT read here.
acceptance: Check that the cycle is the self-product of the GRAPH of phi and not of its image, and that the r = 0 correction is applied in its explicit form Delta_phi - infinity_1.
Check the scaling behaviour under omega_A -> lambda omega_A, which fixes the normalisation of the period Omega_p.
Check that the analytic side is a special value OUTSIDE the interpolation range, not a derivative; conflating it with a p-adic height derivative formula would be an error.

sources.excerpt: These generalized Heegner cycles are naturally indexed by isogenies phi : A -> A'. The cycle attached to phi, denoted Delta_phi, is supported on the fiber (A')^r x A^r above a point of C attached to A', and is essentially equal to the r-fold self-product of the graph of phi. Section 2.3 defines the cycles Delta_phi precisely and establishes some of their basic properties. In particular, it shows that generalized Heegner cycles are homologically trivial.

sources.excerpt: The generalized Heegner cycles Delta_phi are all defined over abelian extensions of K. More precisely, if (phi, A') belongs to Isog_c(A), then the associated cycles can be defined over the compositum of the abelian extension H-tilde/K over which the isomorphism class of (A, t_A) is defined with the ring class field H_c of conductor c. When r = 0, the generalized Heegner cycle Delta_phi is a CM point on the modular curve C. In this case, we replace Delta_phi by Delta_phi - infinity_1, where infinity_1 is any cusp, in order to make Delta_phi homologically trivial. The same is true when r >= 1 by Proposition 2.4, which implies that epsilon_X H^{2r+2}(X,Q) = 0. Thus we record the following. PROPOSITION 2.7. The cycle Delta_phi is homologically trivial on X_r.

nodes.title: The local condition at p for the derived classes, and the published corrections to its proof
nodes.statement: Castella-Hsieh's Prop. 7.8 asserts that the collection c^{heeg,dagger} of SPECIALISED generalized-Heegner classes -- the specialisations at chi^{-1} of the classes z_{f,c_n} -- is an Euler system for the local condition L^*, with c^{heeg,dagger}_K = z_f^{chi^{-1}}. Verifying the Euler-system axiom (E5) is what requires Kolyvagin's DERIVATIVE classes to satisfy the FINITE (Bloch-Kato) local condition at p. In the original paper this was deduced from Lemma 7.5 (stated for p > 2r - 1 and p not dividing c, for a place w of K_c above p). THE PUBLISHED ERRATUM RECORDS THREE CORRECTIONS. (i) Lemma 7.5 requires the further assumption that L/Q_p be UNRAMIFIED, in order to use Fontaine-Laffaille theory; the authors state that they do not know whether Lemma 7.5 holds when L/Q_p is ramified. (ii) Since Lemma 7.5 was crucially used in Prop. 7.8, the proof of Prop. 7.8 must instead go through Perrin-Riou's theory; the correct proof has been given by Kobayashi and Ota, Lemma 4.10 of 'Anticyclotomic main conjecture for modular forms and integral Perrin-Riou twists'. (iii) In Lemma 7.10, 'a p-ramified extension' should read 'a p-ramified ABELIAN extension'. The revised version of the paper carries a footnote to the same effect: the argument given there 'is false since Lemma 7.5 only applies to absolute unramified extensions'.
hypotheses: Lemma 7.5 as PRINTED assumes p > 2r - 1, p not dividing c, and that L'/L/K_{c,w} are finite unramified extensions -- unramifiedness RELATIVE to K_{c,w}. The erratum adds the stronger ABSOLUTE requirement that L/Q_p be unramified, which is what makes the Fontaine-Laffaille description of H^1_f (via [BK90, Lem. 4.5(c)]) applicable; the distinction between relative and absolute unramifiedness is exactly where the original argument fails
the authors explicitly do NOT know whether Lemma 7.5 holds for ramified L/Q_p, so the original argument must not be silently extended to ramified coefficients

Prop. 7.8's conclusion survives, but only via the Kobayashi-Ota Perrin-Riou argument; a decomposition that cites Castella-Hsieh Lemma 7.5 for ramified coefficients is citing a statement the authors withdraw
Lemma 7.10 concerns p-ramified ABELIAN extensions only
proofSteps: The erratum itself gives the corrections; no new proof is supplied there.

The replacement proof of Prop. 7.8 is Kobayashi-Ota Lemma 4.10 (the revised Castella-Hsieh footnote cites [KO18, Lemma 5.7] for the correct argument, while the erratum cites [KO20, Lemma 4.10]; the two numberings refer to different versions of the same Kobayashi-Ota paper).

Remark 4.8 of Castella-Hsieh records, independently of Sec. 7, that the classes z_{f,chi,c} lie in the Bloch-Kato Selmer group by Nekovar Thm. 3.3.1, so the BOTTOM class's local condition does not depend on Lemma 7.5; it is the DERIVED classes whose local condition at p needed the corrected argument.
acceptance: Check every use of Castella-Hsieh Lemma 7.5 for the unramifiedness hypothesis; the stage text is explicit that the original proof must not be extended to ramified coefficients.
Check that Prop. 7.8 is cited together with the Kobayashi-Ota replacement, or else that the statement is restricted to the unramified range.
Check the two different Kobayashi-Ota lemma numbers (4.10 in the erratum, 5.7 in the paper's footnote) and confirm which version is being used.
Check that Remark 4.8's Nekovar-based statement about the bottom class is logically independent of Lemma 7.5.

sources.excerpt: Lemma 7.5: We have to assume further L/Q_p to be unramified in the proof in order to use Fontaine-Laffaille theory, and we do not know if Lemma 7.5 holds when L/Q_p is ramified. This lemma was crucially used in Prop. 7.8 to conclude the Kolyvagin's derivative classes satisfy the local condition at p, which one can instead use Perrin-Riou's theory to verify. The correct proof of Prop. 7.8 has been given in a work of Kobayashi and Ota [KO20, Lemma 4.10].

sources.excerpt: Lemma 7.5. Suppose p > 2r - 1 and p not dividing c. Let w be a place of K_c above p, and let K_{c,w} be the completion of K_c at w. If L'/L/K_{c,w} are finite unramified extensions, then the corestriction map cor_{L'/L} : H^1_f(L', T_M tensor chi) -> H^1_f(L, T_M tensor chi) is surjective, and the restriction map res_{L,L'} : H^1(L, T_M tensor chi^{-1})/H^1_f(L, T_M tensor chi^{-1}) -> H^1(L', T_M tensor chi^{-1})/H^1_f(L', T_M tensor chi^{-1}) is injective. ... Proposition 7.8. The collection c^{heeg,dagger} in ES(T, chi, L^*) is an Euler system for the local condition L^* with c^{heeg,dagger}_K = z_f^{chi^{-1}}.
sources.match: Gives both statements as printed, showing that Lemma 7.5's unramifiedness is relative to K_{c,w} (the erratum's extra hypothesis is absolute) and that the Euler system of Prop. 7.8 is the collection of specialised, not derived, classes; added in review.

nodes.title: Castella-Hsieh's p-adic Abel-Jacobi formula (Thm. 4.9) and its Lambda-adic reciprocity (Thm. 5.7)
nodes.statement: THEOREM 4.9: suppose p = p p-bar splits in K; let psi be an anticyclotomic Hecke character of infinity type (r,-r) and conductor c_o O_K with (c_o, Np) = 1. If phi-hat in X_{p^infinity} is the p-adic avatar of an anticyclotomic Hecke character of infinity type (r+j, -j-r) with -r < j < r and conductor p^n O_K with n >= 1, then L_{p,psi}(f)(phi-hat^{-1}) / Omega_p^{-2j} = [g(phi_p^{-1}) phi_p(p^n) c_o^{1-r} psi-hat_p^{-1}(p^n) / (r-1+j)!] times the pairing < log_p(z_{f,chi}), omega_f tensor omega_A^{r-1+j} eta_A^{r-1-j} t^{1-2r} >, where chi = psi-hat^{-1} phi-hat and log_p = log composed with loc_p. THEOREM 5.7: suppose p = p p-bar splits in K, let f in S^{new}_{2r}(Gamma_0(N)) with p not dividing N be a p-ORDINARY newform, and let psi be an anticyclotomic Hecke character of infinity type (r,-r) and conductor c_o O_K with p not dividing c_o. Then < L_{p,psi}(z_f), omega_f tensor t^{-2r} > = (-c_o^{r-1}) . L_{p,psi}(f) . sigma_{-1,p} in Lambda-hat^{ur}_F(Gamma-tilde), where sigma_{-1,p} = rec_p(-1) restricted to K_{p^infinity} is an element of ORDER TWO of Gamma-tilde.
hypotheses: p SPLITS in K as p p-bar; both theorems assume this
in Thm. 4.9 the interpolation range is -r < j < r; this is exactly the range in which epsilon(V_{f,chi}) = -1 (see (6.1)), i.e. the sign is -1 and the classical central value vanishes
Thm. 4.9 requires the conductor conditions (c_o, Np) = 1 and n >= 1; Thm. 5.7 requires p not dividing c_o and p not dividing N
Thm. 5.7 additionally requires f to be p-ORDINARY and of weight 2r (i.e. f in S^{new}_{2r}(Gamma_0(N)))
the right-hand side of Thm. 5.7 carries BOTH the explicit factor (-c_o^{r-1}) AND the group-like element sigma_{-1,p} of order two; an identity stated without sigma_{-1,p} is not this theorem

the t-power convention is fixed by the pairings < ., omega_f tensor t^{-2r} > and < ., omega_f tensor omega_A^{r-1+j} eta_A^{r-1-j} t^{1-2r} >; the exponents of t differ between the two theorems and must be tracked
the coefficient ring on the right of Thm. 5.7 is Lambda-hat^{ur}_F(Gamma-tilde), the UNRAMIFIED completion; the identity is asserted there, not up to an unspecified unit

the sign epsilon(V_{f,chi}) is computed as a product of local root numbers epsilon(1/2, pi_{K_v} tensor chi_v): under the Heegner hypothesis every finite place contributes 1, and the archimedean place contributes (sqrt(-1))^{|2r-1+2j|+|1-2r+2j|}. The base of that power is sqrt(-1), not -1
proofSteps: Thm. 4.9 is proved by a Serre-Tate coordinate computation: since the Fourier coefficients a_n(f-flat) vanish for p | n, the operator U_p annihilates f-hat-flat, so the associated measure is supported on Z_p^x; Lemma 3.1 then converts the twisted evaluation into a theta-operator expression, and Prop. 3.3 assembles the sum over Pic(O_{c_o}).

Thm. 5.7 is deduced from Thm. 4.9 with j = 0 together with Lemma 5.4 (which gives z^chi_f = alpha^{-n} z_{f,chi} for the chi-specialisation) and Thm. 5.1 (the interpolation property of the Lambda-adic logarithm), after checking that the epsilon-factor of the p-adic Galois character phi-hat_p in the sense of Loeffler-Zerbes Sec. 2.8 agrees with Tate's epsilon-factor: epsilon(phi-hat_p) = epsilon(0, phi_p) = g(phi_p^{-1}) phi_p(-p^n).
The identity of measures follows because the two sides agree at the p-adic avatars phi-hat^{-1} of a Zariski-dense set of Hecke characters of conductor p^n, n > 1.
acceptance: Check the interpolation range -r < j < r and its equivalence with epsilon(V_{f,chi}) = -1 in (6.1); outside that range the relevant sign is +1 and the statement to prove is a vanishing, not a formula.

Check both the factor (-c_o^{r-1}) and the order-two element sigma_{-1,p} in Thm. 5.7; the stage text specifically warns that the revised version includes that group-like factor and fixes the t-power convention.
Check the two t-exponents (1-2r in Thm. 4.9 and -2r in Thm. 5.7) and the self-dual twist relating them.
Check the epsilon-factor comparison epsilon(phi-hat_p) = g(phi_p^{-1}) phi_p(-p^n), which is where the Gauss sum enters.

nodes.title: Longo-Vigni's admissibility hypotheses and the Lambda-adic Kolyvagin-system theorem
nodes.statement: Let Xi be the set of primes p such that p divides 6 N (k-2)! phi(N) c_f, OR such that the image of the p-adic representation rho_{f,p} : G_Q -> GL_2(O_F tensor Z_p) attached to f by Deligne does not contain the set {g in GL_2(O_F tensor Z_p) : det(g) in (Z_p^x)^{k-1}}; Xi is finite. DEFINITION 2.1: the triple (f,K,p) is ADMISSIBLE if (1) p is not in Xi and p does not divide h_K, (2) p does not ramify in F, (3) p SPLITS in K, and (4) a_p is a unit of O_p. Longo-Vigni assume throughout that (f,K,p) is admissible AND, 'for simplicity', that O_K^x = {+-1}, i.e. that K is neither Q(sqrt(-1)) nor Q(sqrt(-3)). THEOREM 3.5: let (T, F_Lambda, L) be a Selmer triple satisfying (H.1)-(H.5) and Assumption 3.2, and set X := H^1_{F_Lambda}(K,A)^dual. If for some s >= 1 the Selmer triple (T, F_Lambda, L_s) admits a Kolyvagin system kappa with kappa_1 nonzero, then (1) H^1_{F_Lambda}(K,T) is a torsion-free Lambda-module of RANK 1; (2) there is a torsion Lambda-module M with char(M) = char(M)^iota and a pseudo-isomorphism X ~ Lambda + M + M; (3) char(M) divides char(H^1_{F_Lambda}(K,T)/Lambda kappa_1). THEOREM 4.12 states that the Lambda-module H_infinity is free of rank 1, generated by kappa-tilde_1. ASSUMPTION 3.2, read in full during the independent review, is imposed IN ADDITION to (H.0)-(H.4) with R = O (where (H.0) is that T is free of rank two over R) and has three clauses: (1) V is crystalline and, for every prime v of K above p, its restriction to G_{Q_p} carries a filtration 0 -> Fil^+_v(T) -> T -> Fil^-_v(T) -> 0 with both Fil^{pm}_v(T) free of rank one over O and inertia acting trivially on Fil^-_v(T); (2) the pairing of (H.4) induces ( , ) : T x A -> (F/O)(1) under which Fil^+_v(T) and Fil^+_v(A) are exact annihilators of each other; (3) the groups H^0(K_{infinity,v}, Fil^-_v(A)) and H^0(K_v, Fil^-_v(A)) are finite for all v dividing p.
hypotheses: all four conditions of Def. 2.1 are needed, and they are NOT interchangeable: (1) excludes the finite bad set Xi and the primes dividing h_K, (2) is unramifiedness in the coefficient field F, (3) is splitting in K, (4) is ordinariness at p

the exceptional set Xi contains p dividing 6 N (k-2)! phi(N) c_f -- so p = 2, 3, the primes dividing the level, the primes dividing (k-2)! and the primes dividing the congruence number c_f are all excluded -- AND the big-image condition on rho_{f,p}
the additional simplifying assumption O_K^x = {+-1} EXCLUDES K = Q(i) and K = Q(sqrt(-3)) in this presentation

the hypotheses (H.1)-(H.5) are Howard's, adapted: (H.1) T-bar absolutely irreducible over R/m as a G_K-representation, ... (H.5)(a) the G_K-action on T-bar extends to G_Q with tau splitting it. Assumption 3.2 additionally requires V crystalline at every v above p, together with the ordinary filtration, the annihilator pairing and the finiteness conditions recorded there
conclusion (3) is a DIVISIBILITY, oriented as char(M) divides char(H^1/Lambda kappa_1); the reverse divisibility is not asserted

Remark 2.2 records that conditions (1) and (2) exclude only finitely many primes, that condition (3) holds for a set of density 1/2, and that condition (4) -- ordinariness at p -- is only EXPECTED to hold for infinitely many p, and then with the proviso 'at least if F is not Q'; Longo-Vigni relate the question to the Lang-Trotter conjectures

This is the source's slip, not the packet's
proofSteps: Longo-Vigni prove Thm. 3.5 by replacing Howard's Props. 2.1.3 and 2.2.8 with their Props. 3.3 and 3.4, using the vanishing A_p(K_infinity) = 0 of Lemma 2.4(3) to prove torsion-freeness as in Howard's Lemma 2.2.9, and then following Howard's Thm. 2.2.10.

The Lambda-adic Kolyvagin system is built in Sec. 4 from the generalized Heegner cycles of Bertolini-Darmon-Prasanna in the variant introduced by Castella-Hsieh, using a universal-norm relation (Lemma 4.2, in the spirit of Perrin-Riou's relations) which the authors state is proved there for the first time, and a compatible family (Prop. 4.5).
Theorem 4.12 identifies the resulting Lambda-module H_infinity as free of rank one on kappa-tilde_1.

nodes.title: Castella-Hsieh's Selmer consequences, including the CORRECTED growth formula
nodes.statement: THEOREM 6.1: suppose epsilon(V_{f,chi}) = -1. Then (1) if z_{f,chi} is nonzero, Sel(K, V_{f,chi}) = F . z_{f,chi} -- i.e. the Selmer group is one-dimensional, spanned by the generalized Heegner class; and (2) the classes z_{f,chi phi} are nonzero in H^1(K, V_{f,chi phi}) for ALL BUT FINITELY MANY finite-order characters phi : Gal(K_{p^infinity}/K) -> mu_{p^infinity}. Part (1) restates Thm. 7.7, which in fact gives Sel(K, V tensor chi) = Sel_{F_BK}(K, V tensor chi) = F . z_{f,chi}, i.e. the Selmer group coincides with the Bloch-Kato one. Part (2) follows from Thm. 4.9 together with the nonvanishing of the p-adic L-function: THEOREM 3.9 reads 'suppose (N_f, D_K) = 1; then for all but finitely many phi in X_{p^infinity} we have L_{p,psi}(f)(phi) nonzero', and its proof selects an auxiliary prime ell prime to p N D_K prod_{q | c^-}(1+q) with rho-bar_{f,ell} restricted to G_K absolutely irreducible, and then invokes [Hsi14, Theorem C]. THEOREM 6.2 (f ordinary at p): if L(f,chi,r) is nonzero then Sel(K, V_{f,chi}) = {0}. Its proof uses that nonvanishing forces epsilon(V_{f,chi}) = +1, hence chi of infinity type (j,-j) with |j| >= r; after replacing chi by chi^tau one may assume j >= r, and then V_{f,chi}|_{G_{K_p}} has positive Hodge-Tate weights while those of V_{f,chi}|_{G_{K_p-bar}} are all <= 0, so by Bloch-Kato Thm. 4.1(ii) H^1_f(K_v, V_{f,chi}) = H^1(K_v, V_{f,chi}) for v = p-bar and {0} for v = p; Cor. 5.8 then gives loc_{p-bar}(z^chi_f) nonzero (the factor e^0_p(f,chi) never vanishes) and Thm. 7.9 -- 'if loc_p(z^chi_f) is nonzero then Sel(K, V tensor chi) = {0}' -- concludes. THEOREM 6.3 (CORRECTED FORM): there is a non-negative integer e such that dim_F Sel(K_{p^n}, V_{f,chi}) = [(1 - epsilon(V_{f,chi}))/2] . [K_{p^n} : K] + e for all sufficiently large n. THEOREM 6.4 (f ordinary at p): ord_{s=r} L(f,chi,s) is congruent to dim_F Sel(K, V_{f,chi}) modulo 2.
hypotheses: Thm. 6.1(1) is conditional on z_{f,chi} being NONZERO; it does not prove nonvanishing

Thm. 6.3 follows by combining Thms. 6.1 and 6.2 with the nonvanishing of the p-adic L-function.
